title: In Your Handwriting
prompt:
[Intro: solo piano, slow rolling chords]

[Verse 1: female alto, quiet and close]
There's a note in my locker from the seventh grade
There's a text I should've deleted, and I saved
There's a list in my own writing on the mirror in my head
Every line starts "not enough," and that's the one I've read

[Chorus: full voice, strings and soft choir]
But I found my name in your handwriting
And it didn't say what theirs did
It said "wanted," it said "mine"
It said "worth it," underlined
I keep reading it and crying
My name, in your handwriting

[Verse 2: voice steadier, piano and cello]
They say you only wrote one time, in the dust, with your hand
While a crowd held their stones and a woman couldn't stand
Whatever it was you wrote there, every stone hit the ground
And you told her what you're telling me right now

[Chorus: full voice, strings and soft choir]
And I found my name in your handwriting
And it didn't say what theirs did
It said "wanted," it said "mine"
It said "worth it," underlined
I keep reading it and crying
My name, in your handwriting

[Bridge: builds from a whisper to a belt]
And the hand that wrote it has a scar straight through
So I know what it cost you to write what you do
Jesus, write it deeper, write it where I'll see
Over every other word they ever wrote on me

[Final Chorus: biggest, choir and full band]
I found my name in your handwriting
And it didn't say what theirs did
It said "wanted," it said "mine"
It said "worth it," underlined
I keep reading it and crying
My name, in your handwriting

[Outro: piano alone, last line whispered]
My name. In your handwriting.
style: Modern soul-pop piano ballad in 6/8, smoky low female alto vocal with a catch in it, almost whispered verses, full open choruses, a long climb to one belted line in the bridge and a whispered ending, 72 BPM, F major, slow rolling build, grand piano, cello, string section, soft deep drums from the second chorus, small choir, close warm natural mix, vulnerable, tender, overwhelming
